# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 2. Dashboard > Search bar — step-by-step

### Search bar — step-by-step

The search bar lives in the main body. Its placeholder is Start by typing [e.g. Players with field goals made > 25].

- Above the search input there are two toggles: Player and Team. Click Player to query player stats; click Team to query team stats.
- When Player is active, the placeholder reads Players with field goals made > 25.
- When Team is active, the placeholder reads Teams with field goals made > 25.
- Click into the search bar and type a natural-language query, e.g. Players with points per game > 20.
- Press Enter or click Search to submit.
- On success, the app navigates to the Search Result Screen and shows Results found (or a transient Searching... state).
- If the field is empty when Enter is pressed, the system shows a warning ("please search something").

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 2. Dashboard > Search bar — step-by-step

### Search bar — step-by-step

The search bar lives in the main body. Its placeholder is Start by typing [e.g. Players with field goals made > 25].

- Above the search input there are two toggles: Player and Team. Click Player to query player stats; click Team to query team stats.
- When Player is active, the placeholder reads Players with field goals made > 25.
- When Team is active, the placeholder reads Teams with field goals made > 25.
- Click into the search bar and type a natural-language query, e.g. Players with points per game > 20.
- Press Enter or click Search to submit.
- On success, the app navigates to the Search Result Screen and shows Results found (or a transient Searching... state).
- If the field is empty when Enter is pressed, the system shows a warning ("please search something").

Source: Navigation-Guide.md

## Types of Queries You Can Use

- Basic Query: Simple lookups (e.g., "Who had 10+ points?")
- Complex Query: Combining multiple conditions or filters (e.g., "Juniors with 20+ points and 10+ rebounds against Duke")
- Record Query: Finding the best or worst (e.g., "Highest points in a game" or "Who has the record for assists?")
- Last Time Was (LTW): Looking up history (e.g., "Last time a team had 50+ rebounds?")
- Streak Query: Finding consecutive performance (e.g., "3+ consecutive games with a touchdown")

[7] Stat-Search-Guide.md | How to Search for Sports Stats: The Complete Guide > How to Search for Queries | kind=prose | system=rag
elevant to the period you are analyzing.
- Example: "Lowest turnovers by the team in a season"

- Last Time When (LTW): This functions as a historical marker to tell you the most recent date a specific event occurred. It helps put modern performances into perspective by showing exactly how long it has been since a player or team achieved a similar feat. Just start by typing "last time"
- Example: "Last time my team had more than 8 turnovers in a season"

- Streak Queries: Use words like "consecutive games" or "straight games”.
- Example: "3+ consecutive games with 2+ blocks"

You can use these symbols and words in any search to get even more control:
- > (Greater Than): "Players with > 25 points"
- >= or + (Greater Than or Equal To): "Teams with >= 5 blocks" (You can also just use + like 5+)
- < (Less Than): "quarters in which team scored 2+ turnovers"
- <= or -(Less Than or Equal To): "3+ consecutive games with < 3 turnovers"
- = (Equal To): "Players with = 10 rebounds"
- AND (Both must be true): "20+ points AND 10+ rebounds"
- OR (Either can be true): "10+ assists OR 5+ steals"

#### 3.4.2 Visualize Data

The "Visualize Data" feature adds simple visual representations to search results. After performing a search, users can click the "Visualize Data" button near the results table to display a chart based on the selected query and relevant period (game or season).

Simple: For basic queries (e.g., "players with rushing yards > 50"), a horizontal bar chart shows the top 10 players who met the condition the most number of times. No. of occurrences shows how often each player achieved the stat.
Complex: For queries with more than one condition (e.g., "players with rushing yards > 50 and passing yards > 10"), a scatter plot shows the top 10 players who met both conditions most frequently.

Records (Min & Max): For record-based queries (e.g., "highest rushing yards in a game"), a line chart takes the first 10 entries from the results table (even if the same player appears more than once) and plots each player's record game in the center, with up to 3 games before and 3 games after.

Last Time When: In last time when queries, a line chart picks the unique players from the results and plots up to 10 of their games.

## Types of Queries You Can Use

- Basic Query: Simple lookups (e.g., "Who had 10+ points?")
- Complex Query: Combining multiple conditions or filters (e.g., "Juniors with 20+ points and 10+ rebounds against Duke")
- Record Query: Finding the best or worst (e.g., "Highest points in a game" or "Who has the record for assists?")
- Last Time Was (LTW): Looking up history (e.g., "Last time a team had 50+ rebounds?")
- Streak Query: Finding consecutive performance (e.g., "3+ consecutive games with a touchdown")

elevant to the period you are analyzing.
- Example: "Lowest turnovers by the team in a season"

- Last Time When (LTW): This functions as a historical marker to tell you the most recent date a specific event occurred. It helps put modern performances into perspective by showing exactly how long it has been since a player or team achieved a similar feat. Just start by typing "last time"
- Example: "Last time my team had more than 8 turnovers in a season"

- Streak Queries: Use words like "consecutive games" or "straight games”.
- Example: "3+ consecutive games with 2+ blocks"

You can use these symbols and words in any search to get even more control:
- > (Greater Than): "Players with > 25 points"
- >= or + (Greater Than or Equal To): "Teams with >= 5 blocks" (You can also just use + like 5+)
- < (Less Than): "quarters in which team scored 2+ turnovers"
- <= or -(Less Than or Equal To): "3+ consecutive games with < 3 turnovers"
- = (Equal To): "Players with = 10 rebounds"
- AND (Both must be true): "20+ points AND 10+ rebounds"
- OR (Either can be true): "10+ assists OR 5+ steals"

How to write queries: https://search.athlytesports.com/info/query_builder_updated.html

- Complex Search: Combining 1 to 3 different stats in one search.
- Example: "Teams with 20+ passing attempts and 3+ field goals made in a game."
- Record Search (Maximums & Minimums): Finding the highest or lowest values ever recorded.
- Example: "Highest number of touchdowns scored" or "Lowest turnovers by a guard in a season."
- Last Time When (LTW): Looking up the history of a specific event.
- Example: "Last time any team had at least 3 touchdowns in a game."
- Streak Search: Tracking consecutive performances over multiple games.
- Example: "Players with 12+ receiving yards over 6 consecutive games."

#### 3.4.2 Visualize Data

The "Visualize Data" feature adds simple visual representations to search results. After performing a search, users can click the "Visualize Data" button near the results table to display a chart based on the selected query and relevant period (game or season).

Simple: For basic queries (e.g., "players with rushing yards > 50"), a horizontal bar chart shows the top 10 players who met the condition the most number of times. No. of occurrences shows how often each player achieved the stat.
Complex: For queries with more than one condition (e.g., "players with rushing yards > 50 and passing yards > 10"), a scatter plot shows the top 10 players who met both conditions most frequently.

Records (Min & Max): For record-based queries (e.g., "highest rushing yards in a game"), a line chart takes the first 10 entries from the results table (even if the same player appears more than once) and plots each player's record game in the center, with up to 3 games before and 3 games after.

Last Time When: In last time when queries, a line chart picks the unique players from the results and plots up to 10 of their games.

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 7. Player Dashboard > 7.1 Player Statistics tab

### 7.1 Player Statistics tab

- Click PLAYER STATISTICS in the header.
- The body shows a table with SEASON and one column per stat.
- Filter the data using three dropdowns at the top of the table:
- Select Season — pick one or more seasons to limit the rows.
- Select Category — pick a stat category (e.g. Passing, Rushing).
- Select Substat — pick specific stats within the category. Multi-select supported.
- Click any column header to sort the table.
- The TOTAL row at the bottom of the table reflects the cumulative values for the visible rows.
- All decimal values are rounded to two decimal places.
- To clear a selection: click the x next to the selected value (clearing a category also clears its substats; clearing the season resets the table to defaults).

#### Step-by-Step Navigation

1. Search for a query (e.g., `teams with more than 30 points in a game`).
2. From the results table, click the hyperlinked team name in the TEAM column to open that team's dashboard.
3. Click TEAM STATISTICS to view the team's aggregate stats by season.
4. Click TEAM RECORDS to view the team's performance records with rankings, game dates, and opponents.
5. Click SEASON HIGHS to view the highest value the team recorded for each stat within a season.
6. Click TEAM GAME LOGS to view a game-by-game list of results, scores, and stats.
7. Click TEAM STREAKS to query consecutive-game streaks for any stat threshold.

## How to Search for Queries

Searching for stats is super easy! Just talk to the search bar like you're asking a friend a question. Here is how to use each type:

- Basic Queries: Basic stat search focuses on finding specific entities, like players or teams, that have reached a certain numerical threshold. Use these when you just want to know who hit a certain number.
- Example: "Players with 10+ assists"

- Complex Queries: These are for when you want to be super specific. Complex search can be performed by combining two different stats with "AND" or "OR" to see who met both requirements.
- Example: "Juniors with 20+ points and 10+ rebounds against UConn"

- Record Queries: Record Queries are designed to identify the absolute "best" or "worst" performance metrics within a specific category or timeframe. To execute these effectively, use directional qualifiers like "Highest", "Lowest", or "Most" to define your intended outcome, and always include a contextual scope—such as "in a game" or "in a season"—to ensure the returned data is relevant to the period you are analyzing.
- Example: "Lowest turnovers by the team in a season"

- Last Time When (LTW): This functions as a historical

## Types of Queries You Can Use

- Basic Query: Simple lookups (e.g., "Who had 10+ points?")
- Complex Query: Combining multiple conditions or filters (e.g., "Juniors with 20+ points and 10+ rebounds against Duke")
- Record Query: Finding the best or worst (e.g., "Highest points in a game" or "Who has the record for assists?")
- Last Time Was (LTW): Looking up history (e.g., "Last time a team had 50+ rebounds?")
- Streak Query: Finding consecutive performance (e.g., "3+ consecutive games with a touchdown")

## Search Power Tools: Qualifiers

You can narrow down your results using specific filters directly in your search text:

- Team & Opponent: Filter by team name, conference (e.g., SEC, ACC), or division.
- Player Attributes: Filter by player name, class (Freshman, Sophomore, Junior, Senior), or position (QB, RB, Guard, etc.).
- Game Context: Search by game result (Win/Loss) or game type (Regular season vs. Post-season).

### Differences from Player view

- The toggle on the Dashboard must be set to Team before submitting the query.
- Some filters that apply only to players (Position) will be hidden.
- The "Career" period is not offered for Team queries — Team queries support Game, Half, Quarter, and Season periods only.

## 2. Scope

The Athlyte Search Feature is designed to enable a natural language search interface for sports data and statistics. It supports queries related to entities like player and team performance across sports like
- Men’s Football (MFB)
- Men’s Basketball (MBB)
- Women’s Basketball (WBB)
- Men’s Ice Hockey (MIH)
- Women’s Ice Hockey (WIH)
- Men’s Soccer (MSO)
- Women’s Soccer (WSO)
- Men’s Volleyball (MVB)
- Women’s Volleyball (WVB)
It includes:
- Integration with primary data sources (Genius and Recordbook).
- Supported sports, entities, query types, and data periods.
- Data processing, normalization, and known reliability aspects.
- Key application modules and background data processing flows.

The Ask Athlyte Bot is a sports analytics assistant integrated into the platform. It helps users explore stats, frame sports queries effectively to get the best results from the Athlyte search feature, and answer any questions about how to use the platform.

# Athlyte Search User Guide > Athlyte Search Overview

## Athlyte Search Overview

Athlyte Search is a natural language interface that allows you to find sports data by simply typing questions or statements. Instead of navigating complex databases, you can search for player and team performances across Men’s Football (MFB), Men’s Basketball (MBB), and Women’s Basketball (WBB).

Source: Athlyte-Search-User-Guide.md

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 2. Dashboard > Profile dropdown — step-by-step

### Profile dropdown — step-by-step

- Click the profile element at the top-right (the username + dropdown arrow).
- The dropdown appears containing three items:
- Dashboard — clicking returns to Dashboard
- Profile — opens the profile dashboard showing account details, current subscription plan, active sports, and options to upgrade (add new sports or add-ons).
- Sign out — clicking logs the user out and redirects to Login
- To sign out: click profile → click Sign out → wait for the URL to change to Login.

Source: Navigation-Guide.md

[5] guides/navigation_guide_md_athlyte_search_navigation_guide_6_search_result_screen_team_.md | Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 6. Search Result Screen — Team > Differences from Player view | kind=okf_guide | system=okf
# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 6. Search Result Screen — Team > Differences from Player view

### Differences from Player view

- The toggle on the Dashboard must be set to Team before submitting the query.
- Some filters that apply only to players (Position) will be hidden.
- The "Career" period is not offered for Team queries — Team queries support Game, Half, Quarter, and Season periods only.

Source: Navigation-Guide.md

Athlyte Search is a natural language interface that allows you to find sports data by simply typing questions or statements. Instead of navigating complex databases, you can search for player and team performances across Men’s Football (MFB), Men’s Basketball (MBB), and Women’s Basketball (WBB).

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 2. Dashboard > Profile dropdown — step-by-step

### Profile dropdown — step-by-step

- Click the profile element at the top-right (the username + dropdown arrow).
- The dropdown appears containing three items:
- Dashboard — clicking returns to Dashboard
- Profile — opens the profile dashboard showing account details, current subscription plan, active sports, and options to upgrade (add new sports or add-ons).
- Sign out — clicking logs the user out and redirects to Login
- To sign out: click profile → click Sign out → wait for the URL to change to Login.

Source: Navigation-Guide.md

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 2. Dashboard > Search bar — step-by-step

### Search bar — step-by-step

The search bar lives in the main body. Its placeholder is Start by typing [e.g. Players with field goals made > 25].

- Above the search input there are two toggles: Player and Team. Click Player to query player stats; click Team to query team stats.
- When Player is active, the placeholder reads Players with field goals made > 25.
- When Team is active, the placeholder reads Teams with field goals made > 25.
- Click into the search bar and type a natural-language query, e.g. Players with points per game > 20.
- Press Enter or click Search to submit.
- On success, the app navigates to the Search Result Screen and shows Results found (or a transient Searching... state).
- If the field is empty when Enter is pressed, the system shows a warning ("please search something").

Source: Navigation-Guide.md

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 2. Dashboard > Sport switcher — step-by-step

### Sport switcher — step-by-step

- Locate the sport buttons in the header navigation (Football, Basketball, Ice Hockey, Soccer, Volleyball).
- Click Football to switch to MFB stats.
- Click Basketball to expand into MBB sub-options. If sub-buttons appear, click Basketball (M) or Basketball (W) to choose the variant.
- Click Ice Hockey to expand into MBB sub-options. If sub-buttons appear, click Ice Hockey (M) or Ice Hockey (W) to choose the variant.
- Click Soccer to expand into MBB sub-options. If sub-buttons appear, click Soccer(M) or Soccer(W) to choose the variant.
- Click Volleyball to expand into MBB sub-options. If sub-buttons appear, click Volleyball (M) or Volleyball(W) to choose the variant.
- After switching, the search bar placeholder updates and Trending/Recent Searches re-populate for the selected sport.

Source: Navigation-Guide.md

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 7. Player Dashboard > Step-by-step navigation

### Step-by-step navigation

- Search for a query (e.g., "players with more than 2 touchdowns in a game")
- From the results table, click the hyperlinked player name in the PLAYER column to open that player dashboard.
- Click PLAYER STATISTICS to view the player's aggregate stats by season.
- Click PLAYER RECORDS to view the player's game, season, and career records with rankings.
- Click SEASON AND CAREER HIGHS to view the highest value the player has recorded for each stat.
- Click PLAYER GAME LOG to view a game-by-game breakdown of the player's performance.
- Click PLAYER STREAKS to query consecutive-game streaks for any stat threshold.

Source: Navigation-Guide.md

# Athlyte Search User Guide > Athlyte Search Overview

## Athlyte Search Overview

Athlyte Search is a natural language interface that allows you to find sports data by simply typing questions or statements. Instead of navigating complex databases, you can search for player and team performances across Men’s Football (MFB), Men’s Basketball (MBB), and Women’s Basketball (WBB).

Source: Athlyte-Search-User-Guide.md

[5] Data-Centre.md | Statistics Data Centre Documentation > Data Availability & Historical Scope > Specific Availability Exceptions > Men's Football (2021 – Present Only) | kind=prose | system=rag
#### Men's Football (2021 – Present Only)

The following metrics were introduced or granularly tracked starting in the 2021 season:

- Defense: Takeaways, Field Goal Blocked by, PAT kick blocked by, Caused turnovers.
- Offense (Teams): Pass Attempts, Times Sacked, Red Zone (detailed scoring/turnover types), Points off Turnovers, 1st/2nd Down Conversions, Time Leading/Tied.
- Special Teams: Net Kickoff Yards, Kickoffs Returned, Net/Average Punt Yards, Blocked Punts/Field Goals.
- Play Direction: Rush Left, Rush Middle, Rush Right.

#### Men's Basketball (2011 – Present Exceptions)

While most basketball data begins in 2009, certain advanced efficiency metrics for teams are available from 2011:

# Athlyte Search User Guide > Query Categories

## Query Categories

You can perform five different types of searches:

- Basic Search: Simple lookups for single statistics.
- Example: "Players with rushing yards greater than 10."
- Complex Search: Combining 1 to 3 different stats in one search.
- Example: "Teams with 20+ passing attempts and 3+ field goals made in a game."
- Record Search (Maximums & Minimums): Finding the highest or lowest values ever recorded.
- Example: "Highest number of touchdowns scored" or "Lowest turnovers by a guard in a season."
- Last Time When (LTW): Looking up the history of a specific event.
- Example: "Last time any team had at least 3 touchdowns in a game."
- Streak Search: Tracking consecutive performances over multiple games.
- Example: "Players with 12+ receiving yards over 6 consecutive games."

Source: Athlyte-Search-User-Guide.md

Clicking on any player's name opens their dedicated dashboard, which is broken down into several powerful sections:

- Player Game Log: A complete list of every game played in a selected season, providing a chronological view of their performance.
- Player Streaks: Analyzes performances across consecutive games to identify consistent high-level play.

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 2. Dashboard > Search bar — step-by-step

### Search bar — step-by-step

The search bar lives in the main body. Its placeholder is Start by typing [e.g. Players with field goals made > 25].

- Above the search input there are two toggles: Player and Team. Click Player to query player stats; click Team to query team stats.
- When Player is active, the placeholder reads Players with field goals made > 25.
- When Team is active, the placeholder reads Teams with field goals made > 25.
- Click into the search bar and type a natural-language query, e.g. Players with points per game > 20.
- Press Enter or click Search to submit.
- On success, the app navigates to the Search Result Screen and shows Results found (or a transient Searching... state).
- If the field is empty when Enter is pressed, the system shows a warning ("please search something").

Source: Navigation-Guide.md

### Understanding the Results

The results are displayed in the main area of the screen:

- Grouped Statistics: Records are often grouped by the specific metric (e.g., "Stat: Passing Yards"). Each group displays a table of top performers.
- Table Data:
- Entity Name: The name of the Player or Team.
- Value: The numerical achievement for that stat.
- Period (Game/Season): Additional context on which specific game or season the record occurred.

# Search Export & Report Documentation > 3. Viewing Records > How to Use Filters

### How to Use Filters

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 2. Dashboard > Search bar — step-by-step

### Search bar — step-by-step

The search bar lives in the main body. Its placeholder is Start by typing [e.g. Players with field goals made > 25].

- Above the search input there are two toggles: Player and Team. Click Player to query player stats; click Team to query team stats.
- When Player is active, the placeholder reads Players with field goals made > 25.
- When Team is active, the placeholder reads Teams with field goals made > 25.
- Click into the search bar and type a natural-language query, e.g. Players with points per game > 20.
- Press Enter or click Search to submit.
- On success, the app navigates to the Search Result Screen and shows Results found (or a transient Searching... state).
- If the field is empty when Enter is pressed, the system shows a warning ("please search something").

Source: Navigation-Guide.md

# Athlyte Search User Guide > Navigating Your Results > Sidebar Filters

- Game Type: Toggle between Regular Season and Post-season games.
- Date Range: Specify custom start and end dates to see stats from a particular timeframe.
- Player Metadata: Filter by Name, Position (e.g., QB, Guard), or Class year (Freshman, Sophomore, Junior, Senior).
- Period Type: Filter by specific parts of the game like first half or overtime.

### Player Dashboard

Clicking on any player's name opens their dedicated dashboard, which is broken down into several powerful sections:

- Player Statistics: A seasonal overview showing aggregate stats for every year of their career. You can filter these by season and category (e.g., Passing, Defense).
- Player Records: A deep dive into individual game performances. This section shows the player's rank for specific stats and even identifies the "value to beat" for the rank immediately above them.
- Season & Career Highs: Quickly view the best mark a player has ever achieved in a single game, either within a specific season or across their entire career, including the date and opponent.
- Player Game Log: A complete list of every game played in a selected season, providing a chronological view of their performance.
- Player Streaks: Analyzes performances across consecutive games to identify consistent high-level play.

[7] R3-Features.md | R3 Features Overview > Team Dashboard | kind=prose | system=rag
## Team Dashboard

[8] Search-Functional-Documentation.md | Athlyte Search Application - Functional Specification > 3. Detailed Functional Requirements > 3.3 Application Features > 3.3.2 Game Dashboard | kind=prose | system=rag
#### 3.3.2 Game Dashboard

Player Stats
Provides a detailed breakdown of individual player statistics for both teams in the game.

Filters: A "Category:" dropdown allows users to change the type of statistics displayed (e.g., passing, rushing, receiving, etc.).

Team Stats
It provides a side-by-side comparison of various statistical categories for both team and opponent team for the specified game.

Rosters
The "Rosters" tab of the game dashboard, provides a list of players for both competing teams during this specific game.

Play-by-Play
This gives a detailed description of every action, movement, and event of a match.

Filters: A "Show" dropdown allows users to filter the roster between starters and the full roster.

Revisions in R2
- In the new process, data extraction from the record books is mostly automated, with manual intervention required only for verification.
- This process, called the match process, involves manually comparing the extracted data with the data in the record to check for inconsistencies.

Accessible from the search results, this dashboard provides a complete breakdown of a specific matchup:

#### 3.4.3 Typeahead

Typeahead adds real-time autocomplete to the existing search experience. As a user types into the search box, a dropdown appears beneath it showing matching suggestions they can pick from instead of typing the full query.

- Women’s Volleyball (WVB)

## Visualize Data

The "Visualize Data" feature adds simple visual representations to search results. After performing a search, users can click the "Visualize Data" button near the results table to display a chart based on the selected query and relevant period (game or season).

The type of queries supported for this are:

- Simple
- Complex
- Records
- Last Time When
- Streaks

**Simple:** For basic queries (e.g., "players with rushing yards > 50"), a horizontal bar chart shows the top 10 players who met the condition the most number of times. No. of occurrences shows how often each player achieved the stat.

**Complex:** For queries with more than one condition (e.g., "players with rushing yards > 50 and passing yards > 10"), a scatter plot shows the top 10 players who met both conditions most frequently.

### Player Dashboard

Clicking on any player's name opens their dedicated dashboard, which is broken down into several powerful sections:

- Player Statistics: A seasonal overview showing aggregate stats for every year of their career. You can filter these by season and category (e.g., Passing, Defense).
- Player Records: A deep dive into individual game performances. This section shows the player's rank for specific stats and even identifies the "value to beat" for the rank immediately above them.
- Season & Career Highs: Quickly view the best mark a player has ever achieved in a single game, either within a specific season or across their entire career, including the date and opponent.
- Player Game Log: A complete list of every game played in a selected season, providing a chronological view of their performance.
- Player Streaks: Analyzes performances across consecutive games to identify consistent high-level play.

# Athlyte Search User Guide > Query Categories

## Query Categories

You can perform five different types of searches:

- Basic Search: Simple lookups for single statistics.
- Example: "Players with rushing yards greater than 10."
- Complex Search: Combining 1 to 3 different stats in one search.
- Example: "Teams with 20+ passing attempts and 3+ field goals made in a game."
- Record Search (Maximums & Minimums): Finding the highest or lowest values ever recorded.
- Example: "Highest number of touchdowns scored" or "Lowest turnovers by a guard in a season."
- Last Time When (LTW): Looking up the history of a specific event.
- Example: "Last time any team had at least 3 touchdowns in a game."
- Streak Search: Tracking consecutive performances over multiple games.
- Example: "Players with 12+ receiving yards over 6 consecutive games."

Source: Athlyte-Search-User-Guide.md

## Athlyte Search Overview

Athlyte Search is a natural language interface that allows you to find sports data by simply typing questions or statements. Instead of navigating complex databases, you can search for player and team performances across Men’s Football (MFB), Men’s Basketball (MBB), and Women’s Basketball (WBB).

# Athlyte Search User Guide > Navigating Your Results > Game Dashboard

### Game Dashboard

Accessible from the search results, this dashboard provides a complete breakdown of a specific matchup:

- Individual Player Breakdown: Detailed statistical performance for every player on both teams for that specific game. Users can switch between stat categories (e.g., Rushing vs. Receiving) using a dropdown.
- Team Stats Comparison: A side-by-side view of team-level statistics, allowing you to compare how the home and away teams performed across all categories.
- Game Rosters: View the full list of players available for both teams. A toggle allows you to switch between viewing only the starters or the full roster.

Source: Athlyte-Search-User-Guide.md

[8] guides/athlyte_search_user_guide_md_athlyte_search_user_guide_navigating_your_results_p.md | Athlyte Search User Guide > Navigating Your Results > Player Dashboard | kind=okf_guide | system=okf
# Athlyte Search User Guide > Navigating Your Results > Player Dashboard

### Player Dashboard

Clicking on any player's name opens their dedicated dashboard, which is broken down into several powerful sections:

- Player Statistics: A seasonal overview showing aggregate stats for every year of their career. You can filter these by season and category (e.g., Passing, Defense).
- Player Records: A deep dive into individual game performances. This section shows the player's rank for specific stats and even identifies the "value to beat" for the rank immediately above them.
- Season & Career Highs: Quickly view the best mark a player has ever achieved in a single game, either within a specific season or across their entire career, including the date and opponent.
- Player Game Log: A complete list of every game played in a selected season, providing a chronological view of their performance.
- Player Streaks: Analyzes performances across consecutive games to identify consistent high-level play.

Source: Athlyte-Search-User-Guide.md

## Visualize Data

The "Visualize Data" feature adds simple visual representations to search results. After performing a search, users can click the "Visualize Data" button near the results table to display a chart based on the selected query and relevant period (game or season).

- Complex
- Records

The Team Dashboard shows a single team's full statistical profile across five tabs.

### Player Dashboard

Clicking on any player's name opens their dedicated dashboard, which is broken down into several powerful sections:

- Player Statistics: A seasonal overview showing aggregate stats for every year of their career. You can filter these by season and category (e.g., Passing, Defense).
- Player Records: A deep dive into individual game performances. This section shows the player's rank for specific stats and even identifies the "value to beat" for the rank immediately above them.
- Season & Career Highs: Quickly view the best mark a player has ever achieved in a single game, either within a specific season or across their entire career, including the date and opponent.
- Player Game Log: A complete list of every game played in a selected season, providing a chronological view of their performance.
- Player Streaks: Analyzes performances across consecutive games to identify consistent high-level play.

[8] Navigation-Guide.md | Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 8. Team Dashboard > Step-by-Step Navigation | kind=prose | system=rag
#### Step-by-Step Navigation

1. Search for a query (e.g., `teams with more than 30 points in a game`).
2. From the results table, click the hyperlinked team name in the TEAM column to open that team's dashboard.
3. Click TEAM STATISTICS to view the team's aggregate stats by season.
4. Click TEAM RECORDS to view the team's performance records with rankings, game dates, and opponents.
5. Click SEASON HIGHS to view the highest value the team recorded for each stat within a season.
6. Click TEAM GAME LOGS to view a game-by-game list of results, scores, and stats.
7. Click TEAM STREAKS to query consecutive-game streaks for any stat threshold.

### Search bar — step-by-step

The search bar lives in the main body. Its placeholder is Start by typing [e.g. Players with field goals made > 25].

- Above the search input there are two toggles: Player and Team. Click Player to query player stats; click Team to query team stats.
- When Player is active, the placeholder reads Players with field goals made > 25.
- When Team is active, the placeholder reads Teams with field goals made > 25.
- Click into the search bar and type a natural-language query, e.g. Players with points per game > 20.
- Press Enter or click Search to submit.
- On success, the app navigates to the Search Result Screen and shows Results found (or a transient Searching... state).
- If the field is empty when Enter is pressed, the system shows a warning ("please search something").

- Total results count (e.g. 42 Results found).

### Technical Details

- File Format: Results are exported in Excel (.xlsx) format.
- Storage: The file is saved directly to your device's default download folder.
- Content: The export includes all data currently visible in your search results table.

[7] Export-Report-Records.md | Search Export & Report Documentation > 2. Reporting an Issue > How to Submit a Report | kind=prose | system=rag
### How to Submit a Report

- Locate the Button: Click the "Report Issue" button, which is located at the top right of the result screen.
- Describe the Problem: A dedicated window will open. Provide a clear and detailed description of the issue you encountered.
- Submit: Click the submit button within the window.

[8] Navigation-Guide.md | Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 7. Player Dashboard > 7.5 Player Streaks tab | kind=prose | system=rag
### 7.5 Player Streaks tab

- Click PLAYER STREAKS in the header.
- The page shows:
- An Export button at the top-left of the table.
- A Filters section on the left with: Category, Stat, Stat Value, Streak Length, Date Range.
- A View Results button below the filters.
- To run a streak query:
- Click Select Category and choose a category.
- Click Select Stat and choose a stat.
- Click into Stat Value and type a numeric threshold.
- Click into Streak Length and type the minimum streak length.
- (Optional) Pick a Date Range to bound the streak window.
- Click View Results — the table reloads with matching streaks.
- To change the threshold, edit Stat Value and click View Results again.
- To remove date range, click x next to the selected dates.
- Click Export to download the current streak table as Excel.

# Search Export & Report Documentation > 3. Viewing Records > How to Use Filters

### How to Use Filters

To view records, you must complete the following filter selections in the left sidebar:

- Select Type: Choose between Player or Team stats.
- Stat Category: Once a type is selected, choose a specific category (e.g., Passing, Rushing, Scoring). These categories are dynamically loaded based on the selected sport and type.
- Stat Period: Select the timeframe for the record:
- Game: Single-game records.
- Season: Full-season records.
- Career: All-time career records (available for Player type only).

Source: Export-Report-Records.md

### How to Export

- Generate Results: Perform your search or query on the Athlyte Search Dashboard.
- Initiate Export: Click the "Export" button located at the top right side on the results page.
- Download: The system will automatically generate a file containing your current results.

# Search Export & Report Documentation > 3. Viewing Records > Understanding the Results

### Understanding the Results

The results are displayed in the main area of the screen:

- Grouped Statistics: Records are often grouped by the specific metric (e.g., "Stat: Passing Yards"). Each group displays a table of top performers.
- Table Data:
- Entity Name: The name of the Player or Team.
- Value: The numerical achievement for that stat.
- Period (Game/Season): Additional context on which specific game or season the record occurred.

### 8.2 Team Records tab

Details the team's performance records, including the stat name, value, rank, the stat value of the rank above, game date, and opponent team.

- Click TEAM RECORDS in the header.
- Filters: Select Period, Select Season, Select Category, Select Substat.
- Table columns: Stat Name, Value, Rank, Next Rank Value, Game Date, Opponent Team.
- Click a dropdown to expand options; tick a value to filter; click x to remove.
- Click any column header to sort.
- Decimal values are rounded to two decimal places.

# Athlyte Search User Guide > Navigating Your Results > Sidebar Filters

### Sidebar Filters

You can refine your results instantly using the sidebar without re-typing your query. These filters apply to all query types except Streaks:

- Opponent & Conference: Filter by a specific opponent team or an entire conference (e.g., SEC, Big Ten).
- Game Result: Narrow results to only Wins or Losses.
- Game Type: Toggle between Regular Season and Post-season games.
- Date Range: Specify custom start and end dates to see stats from a particular timeframe.
- Player Metadata: Filter by Name, Position (e.g., QB, Guard), or Class year (Freshman, Sophomore, Junior, Senior).
- Period Type: Filter by specific parts of the game like first half or overtime.

Source: Athlyte-Search-User-Guide.md

[2] guides/athlyte_search_user_guide_md_athlyte_search_user_guide_search_power_tools_qualif.md | Athlyte Search User Guide > Search Power Tools: Qualifiers | kind=okf_guide | system=okf
# Athlyte Search User Guide > Search Power Tools: Qualifiers

## Search Power Tools: Qualifiers

You can narrow down your results using specific filters directly in your search text:

- Team & Opponent: Filter by team name, conference (e.g., SEC, ACC), or division.
- Player Attributes: Filter by player name, class (Freshman, Sophomore, Junior, Senior), or position (QB, RB, Guard, etc.).
- Game Context: Search by game result (Win/Loss) or game type (Regular season vs. Post-season).

Source: Athlyte-Search-User-Guide.md

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 6. Search Result Screen — Team > Differences from Player view

### Differences from Player view

- The toggle on the Dashboard must be set to Team before submitting the query.
- Some filters that apply only to players (Position) will be hidden.
- The "Career" period is not offered for Team queries — Team queries support Game, Half, Quarter, and Season periods only.

Source: Navigation-Guide.md

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 8. Team Dashboard > 8.4 Team Game Logs tab

### 8.4 Team Game Logs tab

Lists every game played by the team in a season, including the opposing team, result, and score.

- Filters: Select Season, Select Category, Select Substat.
- Table columns: Game Date, Opponent Team, Result, Score, plus stat columns based on filters.
- Scroll down for page size controls — change rows per page; the table recalculates.
- Apply filters via the dropdowns; click x to clear.
- Click any column header to sort.

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 7. Player Dashboard > 7.5 Player Streaks tab

### 7.5 Player Streaks tab

- Click PLAYER STREAKS in the header.
- The page shows:
- An Export button at the top-left of the table.
- A Filters section on the left with: Category, Stat, Stat Value, Streak Length, Date Range.
- A View Results button below the filters.
- To run a streak query:
- Click Select Category and choose a category.
- Click Select Stat and choose a stat.
- Click into Stat Value and type a numeric threshold.
- Click into Streak Length and type the minimum streak length.
- (Optional) Pick a Date Range to bound the streak window.
- Click View Results — the table reloads with matching streaks.
- To change the threshold, edit Stat Value and click View Results again.
- To remove date range, click x next to the selected dates.
- Click Export to download the current streak table as Excel.

Source: Navigation-Guide.md

# Athlyte Search User Guide > Navigating Your Results > Game Dashboard

### Game Dashboard

Accessible from the search results, this dashboard provides a complete breakdown of a specific matchup:

- Individual Player Breakdown: Detailed statistical performance for every player on both teams for that specific game. Users can switch between stat categories (e.g., Rushing vs. Receiving) using a dropdown.
- Team Stats Comparison: A side-by-side view of team-level statistics, allowing you to compare how the home and away teams performed across all categories.
- Game Rosters: View the full list of players available for both teams. A toggle allows you to switch between viewing only the starters or the full roster.

Source: Athlyte-Search-User-Guide.md

# Athlyte Search User Guide > Navigating Your Results > Sidebar Filters

### Sidebar Filters

You can refine your results instantly using the sidebar without re-typing your query. These filters apply to all query types except Streaks:

- Opponent & Conference: Filter by a specific opponent team or an entire conference (e.g., SEC, Big Ten).
- Game Result: Narrow results to only Wins or Losses.
- Game Type: Toggle between Regular Season and Post-season games.
- Date Range: Specify custom start and end dates to see stats from a particular timeframe.
- Player Metadata: Filter by Name, Position (e.g., QB, Guard), or Class year (Freshman, Sophomore, Junior, Senior).
- Period Type: Filter by specific parts of the game like first half or overtime.

Source: Athlyte-Search-User-Guide.md

You can narrow down your results using specific filters directly in your search text:

- Player Attributes: Filter by player name, class (Freshman, Sophomore, Junior, Senior), or position (QB, RB, Guard, etc.).
- Game Context: Search by game result (Win/Loss) or game type (Regular season vs. Post-season).

### 9.3 How to Search tile

Documents the five query categories — Basic, Complex, Records, Last Time, Streaks — with checkmarks for which support Qualifiers and Periods, and example queries for each. Notes:

- A sport must be selected before starting a query.
- Valid periods are Game, Season, Career.
- Career is available for Player stats only — not Team stats.
- Adding qualifiers is optional; multiple qualifiers can be combined.

# Athlyte Search User Guide > Supported Sports

## Supported Sports

The application currently supports deep statistical searching for:
- Men’s Football
- Men’s Basketball
- Women’s Basketball
- Men’s Ice Hockey
- Women’s Ice Hockey
- Men’s Soccer
- Women’s Soccer
- Men’s Volleyball
- Women’s Volleyball

Note: We are working hard to bring you even more data! Support for additional sports will be added in future updates.

# Athlyte Search User Guide > Athlyte Search Overview

## Athlyte Search Overview

Athlyte Search is a natural language interface that allows you to find sports data by simply typing questions or statements. Instead of navigating complex databases, you can search for player and team performances across Men’s Football (MFB), Men’s Basketball (MBB), and Women’s Basketball (WBB).

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 8. Team Dashboard > 8.1 Team Statistics tab

### 8.1 Team Statistics tab

Displays an overview of the team's seasonal statistics, with aggregate values available for every season.

- Click TEAM STATISTICS in the header.
- The body shows a table of aggregate stats per season.
- Filter the data using three dropdowns at the top of the table:
- Select Season — limit results to one or more seasons.
- Select Category — pick a stat category (e.g. Passing, Rushing).
- Select Substat — pick specific stats within the category. Multi-select supported.
- Click any column header to sort.
- To clear a selection, click the x next to the selected value.

Source: Navigation-Guide.md

### Technical Details

- File Format: Results are exported in Excel (.xlsx) format.
- Storage: The file is saved directly to your device's default download folder.
- Content: The export includes all data currently visible in your search results table.

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 2. Dashboard > Sport switcher — step-by-step

### Sport switcher — step-by-step

- Locate the sport buttons in the header navigation (Football, Basketball, Ice Hockey, Soccer, Volleyball).
- Click Football to switch to MFB stats.
- Click Basketball to expand into MBB sub-options. If sub-buttons appear, click Basketball (M) or Basketball (W) to choose the variant.
- Click Ice Hockey to expand into MBB sub-options. If sub-buttons appear, click Ice Hockey (M) or Ice Hockey (W) to choose the variant.
- Click Soccer to expand into MBB sub-options. If sub-buttons appear, click Soccer(M) or Soccer(W) to choose the variant.
- Click Volleyball to expand into MBB sub-options. If sub-buttons appear, click Volleyball (M) or Volleyball(W) to choose the variant.
- After switching, the search bar placeholder updates and Trending/Recent Searches re-populate for the selected sport.

Source: Navigation-Guide.md

# Search Export & Report Documentation > 3. Viewing Records > Understanding the Results

### Understanding the Results

The results are displayed in the main area of the screen:

- Grouped Statistics: Records are often grouped by the specific metric (e.g., "Stat: Passing Yards"). Each group displays a table of top performers.
- Table Data:
- Entity Name: The name of the Player or Team.
- Value: The numerical achievement for that stat.
- Period (Game/Season): Additional context on which specific game or season the record occurred.

Source: Export-Report-Records.md

### 9.3 How to Search tile

Documents the five query categories — Basic, Complex, Records, Last Time, Streaks — with checkmarks for which support Qualifiers and Periods, and example queries for each. Notes:

- A sport must be selected before starting a query.
- Valid periods are Game, Season, Career.
- Career is available for Player stats only — not Team stats.
- Adding qualifiers is optional; multiple qualifiers can be combined.

# Athlyte Search User Guide > Athlyte Search Overview

## Athlyte Search Overview

Athlyte Search is a natural language interface that allows you to find sports data by simply typing questions or statements. Instead of navigating complex databases, you can search for player and team performances across Men’s Football (MFB), Men’s Basketball (MBB), and Women’s Basketball (WBB).

Source: Athlyte-Search-User-Guide.md

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 8. Team Dashboard > 8.1 Team Statistics tab

### 8.1 Team Statistics tab

Displays an overview of the team's seasonal statistics, with aggregate values available for every season.

- Click TEAM STATISTICS in the header.
- The body shows a table of aggregate stats per season.
- Filter the data using three dropdowns at the top of the table:
- Select Season — limit results to one or more seasons.
- Select Category — pick a stat category (e.g. Passing, Rushing).
- Select Substat — pick specific stats within the category. Multi-select supported.
- Click any column header to sort.
- To clear a selection, click the x next to the selected value.

#### 3.1.4 Athlyte Query Language (AQL)

Here a natural language query is transformed into a structured query language (Athlyte Query Language) that a computer program or database can easily understand and execute to fetch the correct information.
This is the standard format for AQL:
{"query_type": , "entity": , "qualifiers": , "stat_period": , "conditions": , "streak_len": , "periods":, "period_type": }
Example:
User Query: The highest punt returns yards accomplished during a season
AQL : {"query_type": "max", "entity": "player", "qualifiers": {}, "stat_period": "season", "conditions": "s_punt_returns_yards", "streak_len": null, "periods": null, "period_type": null}

## Athlyte Search Overview

Athlyte Search is a natural language interface that allows you to find sports data by simply typing questions or statements. Instead of navigating complex databases, you can search for player and team performances across Men’s Football (MFB), Men’s Basketball (MBB), and Women’s Basketball (WBB).

#### 3.1.4 Athlyte Query Language (AQL)

Here a natural language query is transformed into a structured query language (Athlyte Query Language) that a computer program or database can easily understand and execute to fetch the correct information.
This is the standard format for AQL:
{"query_type": , "entity": , "qualifiers": , "stat_period": , "conditions": , "streak_len": , "periods":, "period_type": }
Example:
User Query: The highest punt returns yards accomplished during a season
AQL : {"query_type": "max", "entity": "player", "qualifiers": {}, "stat_period": "season", "conditions": "s_punt_returns_yards", "streak_len": null, "periods": null, "period_type": null}

## Query Categories

You can perform five different types of searches:

- Basic Search: Simple lookups for single statistics.
- Example: "Players with rushing yards greater than 10."
- Complex Search: Combining 1 to 3 different stats in one search.
- Example: "Teams with 20+ passing attempts and 3+ field goals made in a game."
- Record Search (Maximums & Minimums): Finding the highest or lowest values ever recorded.
- Example: "Highest number of touchdowns scored" or "Lowest turnovers by a guard in a season."
- Last Time When (LTW): Looking up the history of a specific event.
- Example: "Last time any team had at least 3 touchdowns in a game."
- Streak Search: Tracking consecutive performances over multiple games.
- Example: "Players with 12+ receiving yards over 6 consecutive games."

# Athlyte Search User Guide > Query Categories

## Query Categories

You can perform five different types of searches:

- Basic Search: Simple lookups for single statistics.
- Example: "Players with rushing yards greater than 10."
- Complex Search: Combining 1 to 3 different stats in one search.
- Example: "Teams with 20+ passing attempts and 3+ field goals made in a game."
- Record Search (Maximums & Minimums): Finding the highest or lowest values ever recorded.
- Example: "Highest number of touchdowns scored" or "Lowest turnovers by a guard in a season."
- Last Time When (LTW): Looking up the history of a specific event.
- Example: "Last time any team had at least 3 touchdowns in a game."
- Streak Search: Tracking consecutive performances over multiple games.
- Example: "Players with 12+ receiving yards over 6 consecutive games."

Source: Athlyte-Search-User-Guide.md

You can perform five different types of searches:

- Example: "Highest number of touchdowns scored" or "Lowest turnovers by a guard in a season."
- Last Time When (LTW): Looking up the history of a specific event.
- Example: "Last time any team had at least 3 touchdowns in a game."
- Streak Search: Tracking consecutive performances over multiple games.
- Example: "Players with 12+ receiving yards over 6 consecutive games."

## Account Access and Team Onboarding

Access to the application is managed through a simple process:

- Self-Registration: If your college is already enabled, you can sign up directly. Once an admin approves your request, you can log in.
- Requesting a Team: If your college isn't listed, contact us to begin the "onboarding" process. We will integrate your official recordbooks and live Genius data into the platform.

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 7. Player Dashboard > 7.1 Player Statistics tab

### 7.1 Player Statistics tab

- Click PLAYER STATISTICS in the header.
- The body shows a table with SEASON and one column per stat.
- Filter the data using three dropdowns at the top of the table:
- Select Season — pick one or more seasons to limit the rows.
- Select Category — pick a stat category (e.g. Passing, Rushing).
- Select Substat — pick specific stats within the category. Multi-select supported.
- Click any column header to sort the table.
- The TOTAL row at the bottom of the table reflects the cumulative values for the visible rows.
- All decimal values are rounded to two decimal places.
- To clear a selection: click the x next to the selected value (clearing a category also clears its substats; clearing the season resets the table to defaults).

Source: Navigation-Guide.md

# Athlyte Search User Guide > Query Categories

## Query Categories

You can perform five different types of searches:

- Basic Search: Simple lookups for single statistics.
- Example: "Players with rushing yards greater than 10."
- Complex Search: Combining 1 to 3 different stats in one search.
- Example: "Teams with 20+ passing attempts and 3+ field goals made in a game."
- Record Search (Maximums & Minimums): Finding the highest or lowest values ever recorded.
- Example: "Highest number of touchdowns scored" or "Lowest turnovers by a guard in a season."
- Last Time When (LTW): Looking up the history of a specific event.
- Example: "Last time any team had at least 3 touchdowns in a game."
- Streak Search: Tracking consecutive performances over multiple games.
- Example: "Players with 12+ receiving yards over 6 consecutive games."

Source: Athlyte-Search-User-Guide.md

## Account Access and Team Onboarding

Access to the application is managed through a simple process:

- Self-Registration: If your college is already enabled, you can sign up directly. Once an admin approves your request, you can log in.
- Requesting a Team: If your college isn't listed, contact us to begin the "onboarding" process. We will integrate your official recordbooks and live Genius data into the platform.

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 6. Search Result Screen — Team > Differences from Player view

### Differences from Player view

- The toggle on the Dashboard must be set to Team before submitting the query.
- Some filters that apply only to players (Position) will be hidden.

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 4. Game Dashboard > Step-by-step navigation > Via Result Screen

#### Via Result Screen

- Search for a query (e.g., "players with more than 2 touchdowns in a game")
- From the results table, click the hyperlinked date in the DATE column to open that game
- Click PLAYER STATS to view the per-player breakdown for this game.
- Click TEAM STATS to view the team-level box score.
- Click ROSTER to view the lineup of players who participated.
- Click PLAY-BY-PLAY to view detailed description of every play of the match

Displays an overview of the team's seasonal statistics, with aggregate values available for every season.

- Select Season — limit results to one or more seasons.
- Select Category — pick a stat category (e.g. Passing, Rushing).

- Click any column header to sort.
- To clear a selection, click the x next to the selected value.

- Basic Query: Simple lookups (e.g., "Who had 10+ points?")
- Complex Query: Combining multiple conditions or filters (e.g., "Juniors with 20+ points and 10+ rebounds against Duke")
- Record Query: Finding the best or worst (e.g., "Highest points in a game" or "Who has the record for assists?")
- Last Time Was (LTW): Looking up history (e.g., "Last time a team had 50+ rebounds?")
- Streak Query: Finding consecutive performance (e.g., "3+ consecutive games with a touchdown")

## 10. Plans & Upgrade Flow

Reached by:

- Clicking the Upgrade button in the top-right corner of the screen.
- Navigating from the Profile page (username dropdown → Profile → upgrade options).

The upgrade flow is a multi-step wizard: Select Sport → Choose Add-ons → Checkout.

[4] Navigation-Guide.md | Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 11. Checkout Flow | kind=prose | system=rag
## 11. Checkout Flow

Trigger: clicking Continue to Checkout on the add-ons page, or Proceed to Payment / the invoice option from the Order Summary.

[5] R3-Features.md | R3 Features Overview > Payment Process | kind=prose | system=rag
## Payment Process

This guide walks you through how to upgrade your subscription, choose a sport, add or remove add-ons, complete checkout (either by card or invoice), and manage your profile. Follow the steps in order — each section builds on the previous one.

[6] R3-Features.md | R3 Features Overview > Payment Process > 6. Managing Your Profile | kind=prose | system=rag
ence:

- Start: Top-right Upgrade button.
- Pick: Sport → Add-ons (toggle Enable checkbox to drop them) → Continue.
- Review: Order Summary must match your selection.
- Pay: Proceed to Payment (Stripe) OR Generate Invoice (grace access).
- Success: Redirect to search page + on-screen confirmation.
- Failure: Sent back to Checkout.
- Manage: Username dropdown → Profile to view or change your plan.

[7] Navigation-Guide.md | Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 11. Checkout Flow > Option 1 — Pay Directly by Card | kind=prose | system=rag
### Option 1 — Pay Directly by Card

- Confirm the Order Summary line items and total match your selection.
- Click Proceed to Payment. You are redirected to a secure Stripe payment page.
- Enter your card details on Stripe and complete the transaction.
- Wait for Stripe to confirm the payment.

If payment succeeds:

- You are redirected automatically to the search page.
- An on-screen confirmation message confirms that your subscription is active.

If payment fails:

- You will be directed to the Payment Pending page.
- Review your order, then either go back to check out or change the plan and complete the payment.

[8] Navigation-Guide.md | Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 2. Dashboard > Upgrade button — step-by-step | kind=prose | system=rag
### Upgrade button — step-by-step

An Upgrade button is visible in the top-right corner of the screen.

- Click Upgrade. The plan-selection page will open.
- Confirm that every visible button on the page is an active CTA — every button should be clickable and respond when tapped. If a button appears greyed-out or unresponsive, refresh the page before continuing.

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 2. Dashboard > Upgrade button — step-by-step

### Upgrade button — step-by-step

An Upgrade button is visible in the top-right corner of the screen.

- Click Upgrade. The plan-selection page will open.
- Confirm that every visible button on the page is an active CTA — every button should be clickable and respond when tapped. If a button appears greyed-out or unresponsive, refresh the page before continuing.

Source: Navigation-Guide.md

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 2. Dashboard > Search bar — step-by-step

### Search bar — step-by-step

The search bar lives in the main body. Its placeholder is Start by typing [e.g. Players with field goals made > 25].

- Above the search input there are two toggles: Player and Team. Click Player to query player stats; click Team to query team stats.
- When Player is active, the placeholder reads Players with field goals made > 25.
- When Team is active, the placeholder reads Teams with field goals made > 25.
- Click into the search bar and type a natural-language query, e.g. Players with points per game > 20.
- Press Enter or click Search to submit.
- On success, the app navigates to the Search Result Screen and shows Results found (or a transient Searching... state).
- If the field is empty when Enter is pressed, the system shows a warning ("please search something").

Source: Navigation-Guide.md

# Athlyte Search User Guide > Navigating Your Results > Sidebar Filters

### Sidebar Filters

You can refine your results instantly using the sidebar without re-typing your query. These filters apply to all query types except Streaks:

- Opponent & Conference: Filter by a specific opponent team or an entire conference (e.g., SEC, Big Ten).
- Game Result: Narrow results to only Wins or Losses.
- Game Type: Toggle between Regular Season and Post-season games.
- Date Range: Specify custom start and end dates to see stats from a particular timeframe.
- Player Metadata: Filter by Name, Position (e.g., QB, Guard), or Class year (Freshman, Sophomore, Junior, Senior).
- Period Type: Filter by specific parts of the game like first half or overtime.

Source: Athlyte-Search-User-Guide.md

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 2. Dashboard > Profile dropdown — step-by-step

### Profile dropdown — step-by-step

- Click the profile element at the top-right (the username + dropdown arrow).
- The dropdown appears containing three items:
- Dashboard — clicking returns to Dashboard
- Profile — opens the profile dashboard showing account details, current subscription plan, active sports, and options to upgrade (add new sports or add-ons).
- Sign out — clicking logs the user out and redirects to Login
- To sign out: click profile → click Sign out → wait for the URL to change to Login.

Source: Navigation-Guide.md

# Search Export & Report Documentation > 1. Exporting Data > How to Export

### How to Export

- Generate Results: Perform your search or query on the Athlyte Search Dashboard.
- Initiate Export: Click the "Export" button located at the top right side on the results page.
- Download: The system will automatically generate a file containing your current results.

Example Search Queries: Basic: "Players with 10+ net rushing yards" / Record: "Highest net rushing yards in a game" / Last Time: "Last time a player had 5+ net rushing yards" / Streak: "3+ consecutive games with 2+ net rushing yards"
What it Measures: Should be returned by default if the search is "Rushing Yards". The total number of yards gained by the player through rushing attempts, adjusted for any yards lost due to negative rushing plays during the game.

## Athlyte Search Overview

Athlyte Search is a natural language interface that allows you to find sports data by simply typing questions or statements. Instead of navigating complex databases, you can search for player and team performances across Men’s Football (MFB), Men’s Basketball (MBB), and Women’s Basketball (WBB).

## 2. Scope

The Athlyte Search Feature is designed to enable a natural language search interface for sports data and statistics. It supports queries related to entities like player and team performance across sports like
- Men’s Football (MFB)
- Men’s Basketball (MBB)
- Women’s Basketball (WBB)
- Men’s Ice Hockey (MIH)
- Women’s Ice Hockey (WIH)
- Men’s Soccer (MSO)
- Women’s Soccer (WSO)
- Men’s Volleyball (MVB)
- Women’s Volleyball (WVB)
It includes:
- Integration with primary data sources (Genius and Recordbook).
- Supported sports, entities, query types, and data periods.
- Data processing, normalization, and known reliability aspects.
- Key application modules and background data processing flows.

# Athlyte Search User Guide > Search Power Tools: Qualifiers

## Search Power Tools: Qualifiers

You can narrow down your results using specific filters directly in your search text:

- Team & Opponent: Filter by team name, conference (e.g., SEC, ACC), or division.
- Player Attributes: Filter by player name, class (Freshman, Sophomore, Junior, Senior), or position (QB, RB, Guard, etc.).
- Game Context: Search by game result (Win/Loss) or game type (Regular season vs. Post-season).

# Athlyte Search — Navigation Guide > 6. Search Result Screen — Team > Differences from Player view

### Differences from Player view

- The toggle on the Dashboard must be set to Team before submitting the query.
- Some filters that apply only to players (Position) will be hidden.
- The "Career" period is not offered for Team queries — Team queries support Game, Half, Quarter, and Season periods only.

## 2. Scope

The Athlyte Search Feature is designed to enable a natural language search interface for sports data and statistics. It supports queries related to entities like player and team performance across sports like
- Men’s Football (MFB)
- Men’s Basketball (MBB)
- Women’s Basketball (WBB)
- Men’s Ice Hockey (MIH)
- Women’s Ice Hockey (WIH)
- Men’s Soccer (MSO)
- Women’s Soccer (WSO)
- Men’s Volleyball (MVB)
- Women’s Volleyball (WVB)
It includes:
- Integration with primary data sources (Genius and Recordbook).
- Supported sports, entities, query types, and data periods.
- Data processing, normalization, and known reliability aspects.
- Key application modules and background data processing flows.

### Recent Searches — step-by-step

- Scroll to the Recent Searches section on the dashboard.
- Each card is a clickable div containing a sample query (e.g. Players with > 50 Longest Field Goal Made in a game).
- Click any card to auto-populate the search bar with that query.
- To return to the dashboard, click the Athlyte logo in the header.

# Athlyte Search User Guide > Athlyte Search Overview

## Athlyte Search Overview

Athlyte Search is a natural language interface that allows you to find sports data by simply typing questions or statements. Instead of navigating complex databases, you can search for player and team performances across Men’s Football (MFB), Men’s Basketball (MBB), and Women’s Basketball (WBB).
